Marconi — Rome, Italy

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Marconi is a well-established residential and commercial district along the Tiber's left bank, home to the Città dell'Altra Economia and a mix of postwar apartment blocks and university-adjacent housing. Local press has reported street prostitution and urban decay serious enough that the city is installing surveillance cameras in the area, and residents on the Marconi/Portuense border have reported a spate of nighttime car break-ins and part-stripping. These are localized, documented concerns rather than widespread violent crime, so some caution after dark is reasonable while the area functions as an ordinary Roman residential quarter by day.

Frequently asked questions

Is Marconi safe?

Wandroz currently rates Marconi in Rome, Italy as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is Marconi safe at night?

At night, Marconi is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.
